llm.summary: This skill openly patches OpenClaw's local web UI to improve the model picker, with disclosed file changes, same-origin update checks, and uninstall steps.

dimensions.detail: The browser script uses localStorage, sessionStorage, DOM mutation observers, a 1-second UI self-heal heartbeat, and same-origin fetch('./') polling every 5 minutes; these are disclosed and proportionate to the UI patch, though automatic reloads can affect the active page.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The installer uses PowerShell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass, auto-detects the OpenClaw control-ui directory, backs up index.html, copies one packaged JS asset, injects one script tag, and deletes only matching older pcl-model-picker.v*.js assets.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill asks an agent or user to run a PowerShell installer that mutates the local OpenClaw Control UI package; the scope is disclosed, but users should treat invocation as an explicit install/repair/uninstall action.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No scheduled task or OS-level watchdog is included in this ClawHub artifact; persistence is limited to the installed UI patch, browser storage for picker size, and timers while the page is open.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is a two-column OpenClaw Control UI model picker, and the artifacts implement that through a local index.html script injection, browser DOM/CSS changes, account-row hiding, size memory, diagnostics, and update detection.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent or PowerShell command to modify your local OpenClaw Control UI files. Review the target directory before running on a nonstandard install, expect the open Control UI tab to reload after same-origin update detection, and use the documented -Remove command to uninstall. The separate GitHub watchdog mentioned in docs would add scheduled-task persistence and should be reviewed separately before use.
llm.findings:
[RA1] expected: The cited changelog text describes UI self-update behavior and an optional GitHub-only watchdog; inspection found no skill self-code mutation in the ClawHub artifact.
[LP1] expected: The same-origin polling exists in scripts/pcl-model-picker.v8.js and is explicitly disclosed in SKILL.md and README.md as browser-side update detection with no external host or telemetry.
[P2] expected: The flagged PowerShell content is a UTF-8 BOM, Chinese comments, and an idempotent script-tag marker regex; no hidden evaluator instructions or prompt-injection directives were found.
[AE4] expected: The mixed-script content is multilingual documentation, license text, and sponsor text; no secrets, credentials, or concealed instructions were identified.
[SDI-1] expected: Automatic page reload on detected newer same-origin build is real and disclosed; it is a usability risk, not evidence of external payload retrieval or exfiltration.
[SDI-2] expected: The periodic network activity is limited to fetch('./', cache:'no-store', credentials:'same-origin') and parses the local app shell for the packaged script tag before any reload.
[SQP-2] expected: The installation does patch deployed OpenClaw UI files, but SKILL.md and README.md prominently describe the exact operations, backup, uninstall command, and that the GitHub watchdog is not part of this artifact.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad Chinese example phrase still explicitly asks to install ModelSelectorOpenClaw; no artifact instruction was found that would run file modifications without an install, repair, or uninstall intent.
[SQP-3] expected: The authoritative-English license clause is a normal license interpretation statement and has no security-relevant runtime effect.
